# String path parameters are escaped with net/url.PathEscape in the generated
# TemplateRoutePaths helpers, so a value containing URL metacharacters cannot
# corrupt the path. A trailing {name...} wildcard value is spliced without
# escaping (path.Join cleans the result). Parameters named after packages the
# helper body references (url, path, ...) are renamed so they cannot shadow
# the imports.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
muxt check

exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{define "GET /files/{name} ShowFile(ctx, name)"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
{{define "GET /tree/{rest...} ShowTree(ctx, rest)"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
{{define "GET /tags/{tag} ShowTag(ctx, tag)"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
{{define "GET /link/{url} ShowLink(ctx, url)"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
{{define "GET /docs/{path...} ShowDocs(ctx, path)"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type Tag string

func (t *Tag) UnmarshalText(text []byte) error { *t = Tag(text); return nil }

func (t Tag) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) { return []byte(t), nil }

type T struct{}

func (T) ShowFile(_ context.Context, name string) string { return name }

func (T) ShowTree(_ context.Context, rest string) string { return rest }

func (T) ShowTag(_ context.Context, tag Tag) string { return string(tag) }

func (T) ShowLink(_ context.Context, url string) string { return url }

func (T) ShowDocs(_ context.Context, path string) string { return path }
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

func TestPathEscaping(t *testing.T) {
	var paths TemplateRoutePaths

	if got, want := paths.ShowFile("a#b c/d"), "/files/a%23b%20c%2Fd"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowFile(%q) = %q, want %q", "a#b c/d", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := paths.ShowFile(".."), "/files/%2E%2E"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowFile(%q) = %q, want %q", "..", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := paths.ShowFile("."), "/files/%2E"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowFile(%q) = %q, want %q", ".", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := paths.ShowTree("a/b c"), "/tree/a/b c"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowTree(%q) = %q, want %q", "a/b c", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := paths.ShowLink("a/b"), "/link/a%2Fb"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowLink(%q) = %q, want %q", "a/b", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := paths.ShowDocs("guides/intro"), "/docs/guides/intro"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowDocs(%q) = %q, want %q", "guides/intro", got, want)
	}
	got, err := paths.ShowTag(Tag("v/1"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ShowTag returned error: %v", err)
	}
	if want := "/tags/v%2F1"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ShowTag(%q) = %q, want %q", "v/1", got, want)
	}
}

// TestDotSegmentRoundTrip proves the escaped dot segment stays on the route:
// the raw value would redirect to / before the handler could run.
func TestDotSegmentRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	paths := TemplateRoutes(mux, T{})

	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, paths.ShowFile(".."), nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("GET %s = %d, want %d", paths.ShowFile(".."), rec.Code, http.StatusOK)
	}
	if got, want := rec.Body.String(), ".."; got != want {
		t.Errorf("body = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
